walkthroughs.body_html:
Numerical Methods — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Numerical Methods brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Numerical Methods.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Using Newton-Raphson on f(x) = x² − 2 with x₀ = 1.5, what is x₁? (Give to 3 dp.)
The trapezium rule estimates which kind of quantity?
options: a definite integral
a derivative
a sum to infinity
a stationary point

mcqs.q: On a probability tree, how do you find the probability of a sequence of outcomes along one path?
options: Add the probabilities along the path.
5.33, by dividing 80 by 15.
Take the average of the probabilities on the branches.
Multiply the probabilities along that path.
The derivative of 5 is 1 because all constants differentiate to 1.
15, because 15% means 15 units out of any amount.
5.33, by dividing 80 by 15.

mcqs.q: What is the derivative of a constant, like d/dx(5)?
options: 0 — constants do not change with x.
5.33, by dividing 80 by 15.
The derivative of 5 is 1 because all constants differentiate to 1.
The derivative of 5 is 5 because the constant stays the same.
